- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

-<!-- entire-agent:begin -->
-Read .entire/agent-guide.md for this repository's workflow, source inspection, and verification guidance.
-@.entire/agent-guide.md
-<!-- entire-agent:end -->
-## Entire and GitHub together (enterprise standard)
-This section applies to agent sessions on a local workstation with the Entire
-CLI installed. It does not apply to agents that run in GitHub Actions or in a
-provider's cloud, such as the `@claude` workflow, Codex cloud tasks or the
-Copilot coding agent: they commit through their own tools and follow their own
-instructions.
-Entire and GitHub run together, in parallel, at all times. GitHub remains the
-source of truth and the home of the controls (signed commits, rulesets, CodeQL,
-reviews); Entire captures a checkpoint when a commit is made and syncs it when
-the commit is pushed. Work recorded in only one of them is incomplete.
-1. Start the agent session at this repository's root, or at its worktree under
-   `.worktrees/`. A session opened in a parent folder is not attributed to this
-   repository.
-2. Before working, run `entire status --detailed`. If the hooks are missing, run
-   `entire configure --force`; do not reinstall what already works.
-3. Keep the result in files of this repository. Work that changes no file here,
-   such as API-only or console operations, produces no checkpoint.
-4. Commit with a local, signed `git commit`; never through the GitHub API or web
-   editor, and never with `--no-verify`, so that Entire's Git hooks run.
-   `.entire/settings.json` sets `"commit_linking": "always"`, so commits link to
-   the captured session without a prompt.
-5. Never write the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer by hand. The hook writes it; if it
-   is missing, investigate instead of adding it.
-6. Push with `git push`, then prove that the checkpoint reached GitHub:
-   `git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/*'` lists the ID from the commit trailer,
-   and `entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo gh/<owner>/<repo> --json` answers.
-7. Once per pull request, after it is merged, generate a remote dispatch:
-   `entire dispatch --repos gh/<owner>/<repo> --since <author time of the PR's first commit> --voice neutral`.
-   Take that time from `gh pr view <number> --json commits -q '.commits[0].authoredDate'`:
-   checkpoints are created at commit time, before the PR exists. The window can
-   also include other work merged in the same period. Add `--jurisdiction <slug>`
-   when the repository is placed outside your home jurisdiction
-   (`entire auth status` shows the home one).
-   Every dispatch must have a title. The CLI has no title option, so take the
-   newest setup for this repository from
-   `entire api --jurisdiction <slug> /api/v1/me/dispatch-setups` and run
-   `entire api --jurisdiction <slug> -X PATCH /api/v1/me/dispatch-setups/<setup-id> -f "name=<repo> — PR #<number>: <PR title>"`.
-   Use the same jurisdiction slug that generated the dispatch in both commands:
-   each jurisdiction lists only its own setups. In Git Bash on Windows, prefix
-   `entire api` with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`, or the `/api/v1/...` path is rewritten
-   into a Windows path.
-   Post the dispatch title and markdown as a comment on the pull request, with
-   the PR's checkpoint IDs read from its commit trailers; the dispatch must cover
-   them. Entire allows one generation per minute per account: after a rate-limit
-   answer, wait 60 seconds and retry once. "No checkpoints" for this window means
-   step 6 failed; never create an artificial commit to fill a dispatch.
-8. Report configuration, executed-and-proven evidence, and pending items
-   separately.

-# AGENTS.md - cross-review
-Pointer for AI agents working in this repository.
-## Project
-- Repository: `https://github.com/LCV-Ideas-Software/cross-review`
-- Repository visibility: private (operator decision, 2026-10-11).
-- GitHub Pages visibility: public (unchanged).
-- Package: `@lcv-ideas-software/cross-review`
-- Site: `https://cross-review.lcv.dev`
-- Branch: `main`
-- License: Apache-2.0
-## Runtime Shape
-This repository is the source of the cross-review MCP server: API-first
-multi-model cross-review with unanimous convergence gates. Binaries published
-by the package: `cross-review`. The protocol and its tools serve agents only;
-human-facing tools, dashboards and operator identities are not part of the product.
-## Mandatory Gates
-```bash
-npm test
-npm run check
-npm run lint
-npm run biome
-npm run typecheck
-npm run format:check
-npm pack --dry-run
-```
-Regression suites are versioned (`npm run` lists the full set); a change that
-touches a guarded contract must run the matching regression before closure.
-## Release
-Publishing runs on GitHub's documented model: a push to
-`main` that changes the `package.json` version publishes the package to
-npmjs.com through npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC), mirrors it to GitHub Packages,
-and then records the Release with the run's own token. npm generates provenance
-automatically for supported public source repositories; this private source
-does not force unsupported provenance. The repository owns no tagging or policy
-machinery and holds no publishing secret.
-The merge is the deliberate act. A pull request that bumps the version
-publishes when it lands, so a version that must not be published must not be
-merged. The manifest version has to be a plain three-part numeric version,
-never a prerelease: the workflow refuses anything else before deriving the
-`vXX.XX.XX` tag. The push that bumps the version is the push that
-publishes: the manifest version is compared with the one the previous head
-declared, so a push that changes `package.json` without changing the version,
-such as a Dependabot merge, ends as a no-op that says so. Native
-`workflow_dispatch` on `main` can resume an unpublished version after a workflow
-correction. Its required full `before_sha` is a maintainer-trusted comparison
-base from before the version bump, not a verified parent or ancestor; the same
-manifest, tag, registry-absence and newest-version guards apply. A run that dies
-after a registry write is resumed with GitHub's own recovery,
-`gh run rerun --failed <run-id>`, which reruns only the failed jobs and keeps
-the outputs of the ones that passed, so nothing is published twice; the
-workflow refuses to start over a version npm already serves and says so.
-The release checks inside `publish.yml` are business logic with no
-repository-owned regression, by the operator's decision: native scanners
-(zizmor, CodeQL) own workflow security, and the script changes only through a
-reviewed pull request. The regression rule above does not apply to them.
-## Language
-cross-review is an agent-to-agent protocol. Agents natively speak English, so
-every surface of the protocol is English: prompts, tool descriptions, runtime
-and error messages, reports, code comments, test descriptions and these
-instructions.

-- Repository: `https://github.com/LCV-Ideas-Software/cross-review`

-- Branch: `main`

-## Runtime Shape
-This repository is the source of the cross-review MCP server: API-first
-multi-model cross-review with unanimous convergence gates. Binaries published
-by the package: `cross-review`. The protocol and its tools serve agents only;
-human-facing tools, dashboards and operator identities are not part of the product.
-## Mandatory Gates
-```bash
-npm test
-npm run check
-npm run lint
-npm run biome
-npm run typecheck
-npm run format:check
-npm pack --dry-run
-```
-Regression suites are versioned (`npm run` lists the full set); a change that
-touches a guarded contract must run the matching regression before closure.
-## Release
-Publishing runs on GitHub's documented model: a push to
-`main` that changes the `package.json` version publishes the package to
-npmjs.com through npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC), mirrors it to GitHub Packages,
-and then records the Release with the run's own token. npm generates provenance
-automatically for supported public source repositories; this private source
-does not force unsupported provenance. The repository owns no tagging or policy
-machinery and holds no publishing secret.
-The merge is the deliberate act. A pull request that bumps the version
-publishes when it lands, so a version that must not be published must not be
-merged. The manifest version has to be a plain three-part numeric version,
-never a prerelease: the workflow refuses anything else before deriving the
-`vXX.XX.XX` tag. The push that bumps the version is the push that
-publishes: the manifest version is compared with the one the previous head
-declared, so a push that changes `package.json` without changing the version,
-such as a Dependabot merge, ends as a no-op that says so. Native
-`workflow_dispatch` on `main` can resume an unpublished version after a workflow
-correction. Its required full `before_sha` is a maintainer-trusted comparison
-base from before the version bump, not a verified parent or ancestor; the same
-manifest, tag, registry-absence and newest-version guards apply. A run that dies
-after a registry write is resumed with GitHub's own recovery,
-`gh run rerun --failed <run-id>`, which reruns only the failed jobs and keeps
-the outputs of the ones that passed, so nothing is published twice; the
-workflow refuses to start over a version npm already serves and says so.
-The release checks inside `publish.yml` are business logic with no
-repository-owned regression, by the operator's decision: native scanners
-(zizmor, CodeQL) own workflow security, and the script changes only through a
-reviewed pull request. The regression rule above does not apply to them.
-## Language
-cross-review is an agent-to-agent protocol. Agents natively speak English, so
-every surface of the protocol is English: prompts, tool descriptions, runtime
-and error messages, reports, code comments, test descriptions and these
-instructions.

name: pr-stuck-waiting-for-secret-scan-push-after-pr-open
description: "PR BLOCKED com todos os checks verdes e 'Waiting for secret scan to complete for commit <sha>' = o HEAD foi empurrado ANTES do gh pr create e nunca houve pull_request.synchronize; cura: um push com a PR já aberta (amend assinado + push --force-with-lease, ou commit seguinte). Scorecard nunca roda em pull_request. Diagnóstico do Antigravity em 29/10/2026."
metadata:

  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3815f8b0-8c60-4890-93a0-2fcc4c634f88
  modified: 2026-10-29T21:43:30.692Z
---

**Sintoma recorrente (20/10, 22/10, 28/10 e 29/10/2026, em vários repositórios):** PR com os 16 checks verdes fica `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`; `PUT /pulls/{n}/merge` devolve 405; a rule suite do `Enterprise Default Branch Ruleset` (id 20582436) mostra só `require_secret_scanning_alert_resolution: fail — "Waiting for secret scan to complete for commit <sha>"` (às vezes com "Code scanning is waiting for results from CodeQL…").

**Causa (Antigravity, conversa 89dc3293, 29/10/2026):** a ordem `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create`. O push cria a ref antes de existir PR; se nenhum push acontece com a PR aberta, nunca há `pull_request.synchronize`, e o job assíncrono do Secret Scanning do HEAD da PR fica órfão. A rule suite do push "passou" porque foi avaliada contra o `Enterprise Non-default Branch Ruleset` (20613778), não contra o da `main`.

**Why:** o Secret Scanning incremental de PR e os workflows `on: pull_request` (CodeQL, Code Quality) só computam o HEAD da PR a partir de um evento de PR; o push anterior à PR não gera esse evento.

**How to apply:**
1. Ao abrir PR, garantir um push **com a PR aberta**: ou abrir a PR e só então empurrar o commit final, ou, se a PR já nasceu travada, `git commit --amend --no-edit -S && git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>` (assinado, no terminal opx). O `synchronize` conclui o scan na hora e libera o merge.
2. Diagnosticar pela rule suite (`gh api repos/<o>/<r>/rulesets/rule-suites/<id>`), não pelos checks: é lá que aparece a regra que falha.
3. OpenSSF Scorecard (`scorecard.yml`) só roda em `push` na `main`, `schedule` e `branch_protection_rule`: nunca bloqueia PR e só fecha alerta depois do merge. Não esperar Scorecard em PR.
Relacionado: [[blocked-merge-extract-exact-cause-before-escalating]], [[never-create-pull-requests-through-the-api]].

description: "HARD (23/10/2026): o claude-code-action ('@claude', '@claude review') NUNCA atua em PR aberta pelo Dependabot, seja qual for o pedido; o claude.yml canônico da frota exclui o autor dependabot[bot] no if do job."

**Regra:** em PR cujo autor é `dependabot[bot]`, o job `Claude Code` não roda. Isso vale para qualquer `@claude`, não só para `@claude review`.

1. O `if` do job em todo `claude.yml` (cópia por repositório e starter do `.github`) leva `github.event.issue.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]'` no ramo `issue_comment` e `github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]'` nos ramos `pull_request_review_comment` e `pull_request_review`. 2. Ao atualizar o arquivo (bump, starter, nova onda), não remover essas condições.

entire session attach — Attach an existing agent session
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit, or to the commit named by --commit. Use this when hooks failed
to fire or weren't installed when the session started, or to attach a
research session.

How the session is linked follows from two facts about the commit — does it
already have a checkpoint, and is it pushed — the same for HEAD and --commit:
  - It already has a checkpoint: the session is added to it. Git history is
    not changed.
  - It is already pushed: the commit is left unchanged and the link is
    recorded in a new checkpoint, which is pushed right away. The link counts
    once the commit's author attaches it, and names that exact commit: after
    a rebase or amend, attach the session to the new commit.
  - It isn't pushed: the Entire-Checkpoint trailer is added to it, which
    rewrites it and any commits after it on the current branch (their content
    is unchanged). A trailer survives a later rebase. Merges after the commit,
    or a rebase or merge in progress, are refused. If a remote can't be
    reached to confirm the commit isn't pushed, attach refuses rather than
    risk rewriting a shared commit.

attach prints what it is about to do and asks before doing it. Without a
terminal (an agent or a script) it changes nothing and exits non-zero; show
the user what it printed, and once they agree, rerun with --force.

A session can be attached to more than one commit. Each checkpoint records the
turns since the session's previous checkpoint.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

When to use this:
Commits made during a session are linked to it automatically. Use this
only when one was missed: `entire session attach <session-id> --commit <sha>`
(default HEAD). Run it without --force first: it prints what it would do
(rewrite unpushed commits to add the trailer, or record a link to a pushed
commit and push the session transcript) and exits non-zero without changing
anything. Show the user that output and ask them; pass --force only after
they agree to that exact change, never pre-emptively. A link to a pushed

input.title: Publicar AGENTS.md e CLAUDE.md (texto-mestre + seções próprias) e remover as entradas *ignore em 22 repositórios
input.description:
## Decisão do operador (05/11/2026)

Pedido feito junto com a auditoria LCV-557 + LCV-574, mas é uma frente independente: abrir um PR pronto (não rascunho) por repositório para publicar o `AGENTS.md` e o `CLAUDE.md`. Até 05/11/2026 a cópia local desses arquivos não estava sincronizada com o `main` remoto.

Decisões, na ordem em que foram tomadas:

1. **Conteúdo:** "Mestre + seções do repo". Cada arquivo recebe o texto-mestre do workspace inteiro e, ao final, as seções próprias daquele repositório, copiadas sem alteração. Dentro de cada repositório, `AGENTS.md` e `CLAUDE.md` ficam iguais.
2. **Repositórios públicos** (`.github` e `lcv-leo/lcv-leo`): "Publicar igual nos públicos".
3. "Publica tudo e sincroniza a main remota com o local com a decisão que tomei frente as opções que você me deu na primeira vez."
4. "E também remover os que estão na main remota": remover as entradas `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` dos arquivos `*ignore` do `main` remoto. São elas: `.github-private/.gitignore`, os `.npmignore` de admin-app (raiz e `tlsrpt-motor`), astrologo-app (`astrologo-frontend`), calculadora-app, cross-review, mainsite-app (`mainsite-frontend` e `mainsite-worker`), mtasts-motor, oraculo-financeiro e ultrabrain-mcp. Os `AGENTS.local.md` não entram.

## O que fica de fora e o que conta como seção própria

* **Seções próprias:** tudo o que, no `AGENTS.md` remoto, vem antes do bloco gerenciado `entire-agent`, mais a seção `## Running in GitHub Actions` do `CLAUDE.md` remoto.
* **Não entram, porque o texto-mestre já cobre:** o bloco gerenciado `entire-agent` e a seção genérica `Entire and GitHub together (enterprise standard)`. O preâmbulo antigo do `CLAUDE.md` (`@AGENTS.md`, "não duplique conteúdo aqui") também não entra: ele descreve a estrutura antiga, e mantê-lo faria o mestre ser carregado duas vezes.

## Divergência registrada para o operador corrigir no texto-mestre

O passo 7 da seção Entire removida registrava a decisão de 02/11/2026: copiar as linhas `Entire-Checkpoint` na mensagem do squash. O texto-mestre diz que o Entire "preserva os trailers no squash merge". A LCV-542 provou que isso não acontece: no maestro-app #536, o commit `304166f31102c5dd787b06393e1052ea0f51d4a0` entrou em `main` sem o trailer. Os merges desta frente vão continuar copiando os trailers na mensagem do squash.

## Consequência informada (npm)

`@lcv-ideas-software/cross-review` e `@lcv-ideas-software/ultrabrain-mcp` são pacotes públicos no npm. Sem a entrada no `.npmignore`, a próxima versão publicada desses dois pacotes levará o `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` dentro do pacote. Nada é publicado no npm por estes PRs, que não mudam a versão.

"""LCV-577: prepare one worktree per repository with the master text plus the
repository's own sections, and drop AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md entries from *ignore files."""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

WS = Path(r"C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace")
WT_ROOT = WS / ".worktrees"
BRANCH = "claude/lcv-577-sync-agent-instructions"
BLOCK = "<!-- entire-agent:begin -->"
RUNNING = "## Running in GitHub Actions"
IGNORE_ENTRIES = frozenset({"AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md", "/AGENTS.md", "/CLAUDE.md"})
REPOS = (
    ".github-org", ".github-private", "admin-app", "astrologo-android", "astrologo-app",
    "astrologo-ios", "calculadora-android", "calculadora-app", "calculadora-ios",
    "cross-review", "github-operations", "lcv-leo", "maestro-android", "maestro-app",
    "maestro-ios", "mainsite-app", "mtasts-motor", "oraculo-financeiro",
    "programa-android", "programa-ios", "sponsor-motor", "ultrabrain-mcp",
)


def git(repo: Path, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:
    result = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True)
    if check and result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"git {' '.join(args)} in {repo}: {result.stderr.decode(errors='replace')}")
    return result


def remote_text(repo: Path, name: str) -> str | None:
    result = git(repo, "show", f"origin/main:{name}", check=False)
    return result.stdout.decode("utf-8") if result.returncode == 0 else None


def own_sections(repo: Path) -> str:
    """Repository-owned text: AGENTS.md before the managed block, plus the CLAUDE.md
    'Running in GitHub Actions' section. The generic Entire section and the old
    CLAUDE.md preamble are covered by the master text and are left out on purpose."""
    parts: list[str] = []
    agents = remote_text(repo, "AGENTS.md")
    if agents is not None and BLOCK in agents:
        head = agents.split(BLOCK, 1)[0].rstrip()
        if head:
            parts.append(head)
    claude = remote_text(repo, "CLAUDE.md")
    if claude is not None and RUNNING in claude:
        running = RUNNING + claude.split(RUNNING, 1)[1].split(BLOCK, 1)[0]
        parts.append(running.rstrip())
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def strip_ignore(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    raw = path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
    newline = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in raw else "\n"
    lines = raw.split(newline)
    kept = [line for line in lines if line.strip() not in IGNORE_ENTRIES]
    removed = [line for line in lines if line.strip() in IGNORE_ENTRIES]
    if removed:
        path.write_bytes(newline.join(kept).encode("utf-8"))
    return removed


def prepare(name: str, master: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    repo = WS / name
    wt = WT_ROOT / f"{name.lstrip('.')}-lcv577"
    if wt.exists():
        raise RuntimeError(f"worktree already exists: {wt}")
    git(repo, "worktree", "add", "-b", BRANCH, str(wt), "origin/main")
    sections = own_sections(repo)
    content = master.rstrip("\n") + "\n"
    if sections:
        content += "\n---\n\n" + sections + "\n"
    for target in ("AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md"):
        (wt / target).write_bytes(content.encode("utf-8"))
    ignore_changes: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    tracked = git(wt, "ls-files").stdout.decode("utf-8").splitlines()
    for rel in tracked:
        if Path(rel).name.startswith(".") and Path(rel).name.endswith("ignore"):
            removed = strip_ignore(wt / rel)
            if removed:
                ignore_changes[rel] = removed
    return {
        "repo": name,
        "worktree": str(wt),
        "own_sections_lines": len(sections.splitlines()) if sections else 0,
        "ignore_changes": ignore_changes,
    }


def main() -> int:
    master = (WS / "CLAUDE.md").read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
    if master != (WS / "AGENTS.md").read_bytes().decode("utf-8"):
        raise RuntimeError("workspace AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md differ; master text is ambiguous")
    report = [prepare(name, master) for name in REPOS]
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

$ws = 'C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace'
$branch = 'claude/lcv-577-sync-agent-instructions'
foreach ($wt in Get-ChildItem "$ws\.worktrees" -Directory -Filter '*-lcv577') {
    Push-Location $wt.FullName
    $slug = ((git remote get-url origin) -replace '^.*github\.com[:/]', '' -replace '\.git$', '')
    $checkpoint = (@(git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)') | Where-Object { $_.Trim() } | Select-Object -First 1)
    $pr = gh pr list --repo $slug --head $branch --state all --json number,isDraft,autoMergeRequest,headRefOid,labels,state --jq '.[0] | "#\(.number) state=\(.state) draft=\(.isDraft) automerge=\(.autoMergeRequest != null) head=\(.headRefOid) labels=\([.labels[].name] | join(","))"'
    $remoteHead = (git ls-remote origin "refs/heads/$branch") -split "`t" | Select-Object -First 1
    $ref = if ($checkpoint) { [bool](git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/*' | Select-String -SimpleMatch $checkpoint.Trim()) } else { $false }
    '{0,-40} local={1} remote={2} sig={3} cp={4} cpRefOrigin={5} PR: {6}' -f $slug, (git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD), ($remoteHead ? $remoteHead.Substring(0, 12) : 'NONE'), (git log -1 --format='%G?'), $checkpoint, $ref, $pr
    Pop-Location
}

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.
